source: AIDOC-catalogued Khmer farmer leaflet, "Coconut Cultivation Techniques for Farmers", prepared with NGO partners including Santi Sena, Buddhism for Development, and a farmer/agriculture association. Note: this scanned copy ends mid-outline — its own table of contents lists further sections on watering (ការស្រោចទឹក), disease/pest protection (ការការពារជម្ងឺ និង សត្វល្អិតចង្រៃ), and harvesting (ការប្រមូលផល) that are not present in the pages available here.
text:
Basal (starter) fertilizer should be placed in the planting hole at the time of planting, then topped up periodically afterward as the tree grows. Fertilizer is buried in the root zone at a set distance from the trunk base rather than piled directly against it.

The leaflet indicates using both organic fertilizer/compost and a chemical fertilizer supplying nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K, labeled អ៊ុន...ប៉ូ-កា in the source, i.e. N-P-K). For later, established-tree applications, fertilizer should not be piled too close to or too concentrated at any one spot near the trunk, to avoid root burn.

The accompanying diagram shows a fertilizer placement zone offset about 2 meters from the seedling, with the fertilizing pit or band roughly 0.5 meter wide and 0.5 meter deep, labeled 'pit for basal fertilizer application' (រណ្តៅដាក់ជីបំប៉ន).

The source pages available end here; its own table of contents indicates it originally continued with sections on watering, disease and pest protection, and harvesting, which are not present in this scan and would need to be sourced separately for a complete cultivation guide.
